body.translated_text: <s>Sekoddeśa</s> (The Exposition of Initiation)
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kālacakra</s> (the Wheel of Time).

children.translated_text: <s>Sucandra</s> said:
Initiation (<s>seka</s>) is sevenfold, O Teacher, and threefold is the supreme (<s>anuttara</s>) [initiation];
for the attainment of mundane and supramundane accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>), tell me in brief. // Sekod 1 //
The Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) said:

children.text: śṛṇu sucandra sekārthaṃ saptadhā trividhaṃ param /
children.translated_text: Listen, <s>Sucandra</s>, to the meaning of initiation — sevenfold, threefold, and supreme;
I shall tell you by way of an exposition of the movement of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) and the extension [of breath]. // Sekod 2 //
The exposition (<s>uddeśa</s>) in the <s>tantra</s> is threefold, and the detailed exposition (<s>nirdeśa</s>) is threefold;
the counter-exposition (<s>pratyuddeśa</s>), the great exposition (<s>mahoddeśa</s>), and the counter-detailed-exposition (<s>pratinirdeśa</s>) is the other. // Sekod 3 //
The exposition that is [also] a detailed exposition is called the <s>tantra</s>-compilation (<s>tantrasaṃgīti</s>);
and the counter-exposition that is [also] a detailed exposition is the <s>pañjikā</s> (commentary), the word-by-word analysis (<s>padabhañjikā</s>). // Sekod 4 //
And the great exposition that is [also] a detailed exposition is the <s>ṭīkā</s> (sub-commentary), which indicates all meanings;

children.text: abhijñālābhibhiḥ sā tu kartavyā naiva paṇḍitaiḥ // Sekoddeśa_5 //
children.translated_text: but that should be composed by those who have attained <s>abhijñā</s> (supernormal knowledge), not by [mere] scholars. // Sekod 5 //
Thus, purified by the six points (<s>ṣaṭkoṭi</s>) and by the fourfold <s>vajra</s>-yogas,
by the four awakenings (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), by the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and the six families (<s>ṣaṭkula</s>), // Sekod 6 //
purified by the five chapters (<s>paṭala</s>), by the world-realm (<s>lokadhātu</s>) and so forth as accepted,
by the two truths, the primordial <s>Buddha</s> would be [revealed in] the [tantra] called <s>Kālacakra</s> (Wheel of Time). // Sekod 7 //
First, the sevenfold initiation (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) which is the introduction for beginners (<s>bāla</s>) —
threefold by worldly convention (<s>lokasaṃvṛti</s>), the fourth in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>). // Sekod 8 //
My teaching of <s>dharmas</s>, as the <s>Vajra</s>-holder (<s>Vajrin</s>), is by means of the two truths:
by the truth of worldly convention (<s>lokasaṃvṛti-satya</s>) and by the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha-satya</s>). // Sekod 9 //
Water, crown, silk-band, <s>vajra</s> and bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>), the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>),
name, and permission (<s>anujñā</s>) — [thus] initiation is sevenfold, O king. // Sekod 10 //
The purification of body, speech, and mind — two [initiations] for each pair of two;
permission is the purification of <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis); the other [purification] is from the purification of <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and so forth. // Sekod 11 //
Water [initiation] is the purification of the <s>dhātus</s>; the crown (<s>maulī</s>) is the purification of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates);
the silk-band (<s>paṭṭa</s>) is the purification of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); the <s>vajra</s> and bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>) is the great syllable (<s>mahākṣara</s>). // Sekod 12 //
The speech of the <s>Buddha</s> is uninterrupted; the purification of sun and moon together;
the purification of sense-objects and sense-faculties is the unwavering <s>vajra</s>-vow (<s>vajravrata</s>). // Sekod 13 //
The name[-initiation] is the purification of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and so forth; permission (<s>anujñā</s>) is the purification of <s>Buddha</s>[-nature];

children.text: ete sapta sekā deyā vartayitvā tu maṇḍalam // Sekoddeśa_14 //
children.translated_text: these seven initiations should be given after setting up the <s>maṇḍala</s>. // Sekod 14 //
The vase (<s>kumbha</s>), the secret initiation (<s>guhyābhiṣeka</s>), that called the wisdom-knowledge (<s>prajñā-jñāna</s>),
and again the great wisdom (<s>mahāprajñā</s>) — that called knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) [initiation]. // Sekod 15 //
Dripping, dripping, then vibration (<s>spanda</s>), and beyond that, non-vibration (<s>niḥspanda</s>);
by the purification of body, speech, and mind, the three initiations [proceed] in sequence. // Sekod 16 //
The fourth is the purification of <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis), which purifies body, speech, and mind;
the child (<s>bāla</s>), the mature one (<s>prauḍha</s>), the elder (<s>vṛddha</s>), and the fourth is the lord of creatures (<s>prajāpati</s>). // Sekod 17 //
From the touch of the limbs and breasts of the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom-consort), the bliss of the emission of <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind);

children.text: payodharābhiṣiktaḥ sa bālaḥ prāptaṃ yataḥ sukham // Sekoddeśa_18 //
children.translated_text: anointed by [her] breasts, he is a 'child' (<s>bāla</s>), since bliss is attained from that [contact]. // Sekod 18 //
From the striking of the secret [organ], the bliss of the emission of <s>bodhicitta</s> born over time;

children.text: prauḍho guhyābhiṣiktaḥ sa guhyāt prāptaṃ yataḥ sukham // Sekoddeśa_19 //
children.translated_text: the 'mature one' (<s>prauḍha</s>), anointed by the secret [initiation], since bliss is attained from the secret [organ]. // Sekod 19 //
From the striking of the secret [organ] over time, the bliss from the vibration (<s>spanda</s>) at the tip of the <s>vajra</s>;

children.text: prajñājñānābhiṣiktaḥ sa vṛddhaḥ spandaṃ gato yataḥ // Sekoddeśa_20 //
children.translated_text: anointed by the wisdom-knowledge (<s>prajñā-jñāna</s>), he is the 'elder' (<s>vṛddha</s>), since he has gone to vibration. // Sekod 20 //
From the passion for <s>mahāmudrā</s> (the great seal), the bliss born from non-vibration (<s>niḥspanda</s>);

children.text: mahāprajñābhiṣiktaḥ sa yato niḥspandatāṃ gataḥ // Sekoddeśa_21 //
children.translated_text: anointed by the great wisdom (<s>mahāprajñā</s>), he [is so called] since he has attained non-vibration. // Sekod 21 //
He should be known as the lord of creatures (<s>prajāpati</s>), the progenitor of all beings;
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, non-dual, imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>). // Sekod 22 //
He is the <s>samaya-sattva</s> (pledge-being); the <s>vajra</s>-yoga is fourfold;

children.text: kālacakra iha khyāto yogināṃ muktidāyakaḥ // Sekoddeśa_23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kālacakra</s> (Wheel of Time) is proclaimed here as the bestower of liberation for yogins. // Sekod 23 //
One should perform the <s>sādhana</s> (practice) of this very [Kālacakra], with unimagined reflections —
with those signs (<s>nimitta</s>) such as smoke and so forth, with wisdom-images (<s>prajñā-bimba</s>) that are like space, // Sekod 24 //
transcending existence and non-existence, [being] the objects of conditions of one's own mind,
free from all accumulations of atoms and dust-particles. // Sekod 25 //
Smoke, mirage, firefly, lamp, flame, moon, and sun;
darkness, digit (<s>kalā</s>), the great drop (<s>mahābindu</s>), the universal image (<s>viśvabimba</s>), the luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>). // Sekod 26 //
With eyes closed and open, [that] which is not conceptually constructed in the void,

children.text: dṛśyate svapnavad bimbaṃ tad bimbaṃ bhāvayet sadā // Sekoddeśa_27 //
children.translated_text: [yet] is seen like a dream-image — that image one should meditate upon always. // Sekod 27 //

children.text: abhāve bhāvanā bimbe yogināṃ sā na bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Meditation on an image in [what is] non-existent — for yogins, that is not [truly] meditation;
[for] there is neither existence nor non-existence of the mind regarding the image, since the seeing [of it] is unconstructed. // Sekod 28 //
Just as a maiden sees in a mirror-divination (<s>pratisena</s>) [things] born of no [real] substance —
past and future <s>dharmas</s> — so too [does the yogin see] in the sky of reality (<s>tattvayoga</s>). // Sekod 29 //
The existence of this [vision] is not [truly] existence, since [it is] the seeing of a meaning empty of substance;
[yet] from the non-existence of substance, meaning exists — like illusion, dream, and magic. // Sekod 30 //
For in the absence of a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), this arising of properties (<s>dharma</s>) is observed,
like a wish-fulfilling jewel (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) that fulfills the hopes of infinite beings. // Sekod 31 //
In the mirror-divination, the maiden sees the unseen — thieves and so forth;

children.text: tat prādeśikanetrābhyāṃ gatvā paśyanti sādhakāḥ // Sekoddeśa_32 //
children.translated_text: practitioners (<s>sādhaka</s>), going with [their] indicative eyes, see that [likewise]. // Sekod 32 //

children.text: yadi paśyati sadrūpaṃ svamukhaṃ kiṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: If she sees a real form, why does she not see her own face?

children.text: yadi paśyatyasadrūpaṃ śaśaśṛṅgaṃ kathaṃ na ca // Sekoddeśa_33 //
children.translated_text: If she sees an unreal form, why not [also] a hare's horn? // Sekod 33 //
She does not see with other eyes; she does not see with her own eyes;

children.text: dṛśyamānamajātaṃ tat kumāryā jātakaṃ yathā // Sekoddeśa_34 //
children.translated_text: what is seen is unborn — like the horoscope (<s>jātaka</s>) [reading] of the maiden. // Sekod 34 //

children.text: dṛṣṭe bimbe tataḥ kuryāt prāṇāyāmaṃ nirantaram /
children.translated_text: Having seen the image, one should then perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) without interruption,
in the upper, lower, and three <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), through the restraint of body, speech, and mind. // Sekod 35 //
In [the channels] that carry moon, sun, <s>Rāhu</s>, feces, urine, and semen,
born of the constituents of water, fire, void, earth, wind, and <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis) — // Sekod 36 //
The <s>nāḍīs</s> of body, speech, and mind [are associated with] moon, sun, and the shadow-planet (<s>taminī</s>);
they carry feces, urine, and semen — [flowing] in the <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (outbreath) in sequence. // Sekod 37 //
The moon [channel] is body —
of method (<s>upāya</s>); speech is the sun-[channel] of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); and the wisdom-body [channel] is the feces-
<s>nāḍī</s>; the speech-[channel] of the earth is the urine-
carrying [channel]. // Sekod 38 //
The upper and lower mind-<s>nāḍīs</s> are two, carrying the shadow-planet (<s>taminī</s>) and semen;
the shadow-planet [channel] is the mind of method (<s>upāya</s>); that of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) carries semen. // Sekod 39 //
Upper and lower, this sixfold family (<s>ṣaṭkula</s>), through the yoga of body, speech, and mind,
is established in all embodied beings in the form of the limbs of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and method (<s>upāya</s>). // Sekod 40 //
and lower —
by the excess of winds;
in the shadow-planet and semen-carrying [channels] — birth, death, and [intermediate] existence. // Sekod 41 //

body.translated_text: The ill omen (<s>ariṣṭa</s>) in the body and speech <s>nāḍīs</s> — upper

children.translated_text: At the time of birth and death, and in sexual union, the semen-carrying [channel],

children.text: taminī ca vahatyūrdhve saṃkrāntau viṣuve raveḥ // Sekoddeśa_42 //
children.translated_text: and the shadow-planet [channel] flows upward — at the solstice and equinox of the sun. // Sekod 42 //
fifty-six
and a quarter breaths (inhalations and exhalations), O lord of men, // Sekod 43 //

body.translated_text: At the conjunction of the ascendant rising, the equinox flows in the middle;

children.translated_text: plus seventy-five more, [making] six hundred [breaths] day and night,
and twenty-one thousand, plus six hundred more — // Sekod 44 //

children.text: vāmā ca dakṣiṇā nāḍī vahatyūnānanena tān /
children.translated_text: the left and right <s>nāḍīs</s> carry those [breaths], diminishing and increasing;
for three and a half years [each], in a hundred-year [lifespan], the middle [channel operates]. // Sekod 45 //
The left and right [channels], above — moon and sun — [are called] <s>lalanā</s> and the other is <s>piṅgalā</s>;
of the nature of water and fire, they are called the lotus-bearer and the jewel-bearer. // Sekod 46 //

children.translated_text: are called the wheel-bearer and the sword-bearer.
// Sekod 47 //

body.translated_text: Below, [they are] the feces- and urine-carrying [channels], of the nature of earth and wind; the middle <s>nāḍī</s> and the left [channel]

children.translated_text: and <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis),
they are called the <s>vajra</s>-bearer and the <s>vajra</s>-bearer. // Sekod 48 //

body.translated_text: Upper and lower, the middle and left [channels carry] <s>Rāhu</s> and semen; of the nature of void

children.translated_text: The feces-<s>nāḍī</s> [flows] by the moon's path; the urine-carrying [channel flows] by the sun's;

children.text: jātau mṛtyau viṣuve rāge rāhuṇā śukravāhinī // Sekoddeśa_49 //
children.translated_text: at birth, death, equinox, and passion — [the channel carrying] semen [flows] by <s>Rāhu's</s> [path]. // Sekod 49 //
That which is above the navel, the <s>avadhūtī</s>, is the <s>suṣumnā</s>, carrying the shadow-planet (<s>tamas</s>);

children.text: yādhaḥ khagamukhā sā ca śaṅkhinī śukravāhinī // Sekoddeśa_50 //
children.translated_text: that which is below, the <s>khagamukhā</s>, is the <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, carrying semen. // Sekod 50 //
In the navel-lotus, the heart, the throat, the forehead, and the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown) lotus —
earth, water, fire, wind, and void — [the channel] flows in the order of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>). // Sekod 51 //
that [channel]
enters the earth in the order of creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>);
from pericarp to pericarp, in the middle of the <s>avadhūtī</s>, is the going and coming. // Sekod 52 //

body.translated_text: Going out and entering,

children.translated_text: In the navel, the secret [center], and the jewel-lotus — carrying body, speech, and mind;
going out and entering, that [channel] takes the form of dissolution and creation. // Sekod 53 //
The <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, for all living beings, is the carrier of the <s>apāna</s> (downward) wind;

children.text: eṣā strīṇāṃ sukhācchukraṃ ṛtau raktapravāhinī // Sekoddeśa_54 //
children.translated_text: this [channel], for women, [carries] semen from bliss, and at the menstrual period carries blood. // Sekod 54 //

children.translated_text: A <s>nāḍikā</s> carries three hundred and sixty breaths in sequence;
the five <s>nāḍīs</s> carry those eighteen hundred breaths. // Sekoddeśa_60 //
Sixty <s>nāḍīs</s>, day and night—thus the <s>maṇḍalas</s> from the body;

children.text: dalamadhye tataḥ pūrve savye vāme 'pare kramāt // Sekoddeśa_61 //
children.translated_text: in the middle of the petals, then in the east, right, left, and west, in sequence. // Sekoddeśa_61 //
Space and the rest always on the left, earth and the rest on the right, from the other side;

children.text: vijñānādibhavo vāme saṃhāraḥ kṣmādi dakṣiṇe // Sekoddeśa_62 //
children.translated_text: arising from consciousness and so forth on the left, dissolution beginning with earth on the right. // Sekoddeśa_62 //

children.text: apare pūrve dharā vāyuḥ prajñopāyaḥ parasparam /
children.translated_text: In the west and east, earth and wind, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (method), mutually;
by means of thumb and ring finger, whence the consecration into the mouth. // Sekoddeśa_63 //
On the right and left, the oblation water, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (method), mutually;
by means of middle finger and index finger, whence the sword shall come to be. // Sekoddeśa_64 //
The <s>mudrā</s> has a half-moon shape—the fang, the knife, and the little finger;
the imperishable void, above and below, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (method), mutually. // Sekoddeśa_65 //
In the conjunction of the ten <s>maṇḍalas</s>, of the fingers, mutually,

children.text: karatale puṭite mūrdhni ekaśūkaṃ sakartikam // Sekoddeśa_66 //
children.translated_text: in the cupped palm on the crown, a single spike with a knife. // Sekoddeśa_66 //
At the equinox, in the middle <s>nāḍī</s>, causing creation and dissolution;
the unity of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and three <s>vajras</s>, when arrived at the middle. // Sekoddeśa_67 //
When the moon and sun <s>nāḍīs</s> are blocked, the feces-and-urine <s>nāḍīs</s> are blocked;
when the <s>Rāhu</s> <s>nāḍī</s> is blocked, the semen-carrying [<s>nāḍī</s>] below is blocked. // Sekoddeśa_68 //

this is the movement of the <s>nāḍīs</s>, through the three paths of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>. // Sekoddeśa_69 //

an ascent of thirty-three days—the death sign when the sun is in the right [<s>nāḍī</s>]. // Sekoddeśa_71 //

body.translated_text: Having known the signs of death, one should place the <s>prāṇa</s> in the <s>bindu</s>; taking refuge in the state of <s>Avadhūtī</s>,

children.translated_text: One should always perform the <s>vajra</s> rising, from the breaking of the movement of moon and sun;
otherwise the <s>prāṇa</s> wind does not enter the body of <s>Avadhūtī</s>. // Sekoddeśa_78 //
<s>Apāna</s> goes downward in the <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>; death results from its entry there;
this deception of death signs indeed occurs through the blisses of <s>yogins</s>. // Sekoddeśa_79 //
The arrival of <s>śukra</s> (semen) is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), from the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> to the <s>ūrṇā</s> lotus;

children.text: kaṇṭhe hṛdi paramānandaṃ viramānandaṃ tato bhavet // Sekoddeśa_80 //
children.translated_text: at the throat and heart is <s>paramānanda</s> (supreme bliss); then <s>viramānanda</s> (cessation bliss) arises. // Sekoddeśa_80 //
Various delight at the navel, when it has arrived at the secret lotus;
from the secret place to the <s>vajramaṇi</s> (vajra jewel), <s>sahajānanda</s> (innate bliss), imperishable. // Sekoddeśa_81 //
<s>Apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa), <s>mahārāga</s> (great passion), the imperishable lord;
the bliss that falls from dispassion—that is <s>pratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (abiding nirvāṇa). // Sekoddeśa_82 //
The rising of the <s>śukra</s>-moon in the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, fullness in the secret lotus;

children.text: kalā ṣoḍaśamā yā sā maṇipadme vajramūrdhagā // Sekoddeśa_83 //
children.translated_text: that sixteenth <s>kalā</s> (digit), in the jewel-lotus, going to the tip of the <s>vajra</s>. // Sekoddeśa_83 //
Above that would be the time of falling, at the arrival of the first day of the dark fortnight;
the sun quickly goes to its station on the new moon day, from dispassion. // Sekoddeśa_84 //
Its sixteenth <s>kalā</s> (digit) has gone to the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> lotus;
the lost moon is declared here as dispassion from the bliss of passion. // Sekoddeśa_85 //
The lunar nectar goes downward in the death of all embodied beings;
above, the solar <s>rajas</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>-consciousness, characterized by existence. // Sekoddeśa_86 //
Therefore, O king, the lunar nectar must be made to go upward;
the solar <s>rajas</s> below, in the imperishable bliss of <s>Rāhu</s>-consciousness. // Sekoddeśa_87 //
In the <s>ūrṇā</s> lotus of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the full moon of the lunar nectar;

children.text: amārkarajaso guhye kaloṣṇīṣe maṇau tayoḥ // Sekoddeśa_88 //
children.translated_text: the new moon of the solar <s>rajas</s> in the secret [center], the <s>kalā</s> in the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, in the jewel of those two. // Sekoddeśa_88 //
Thus the <s>vajra</s> state of the Teacher is the reverse for all embodied beings;
from <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa), the elements go in reverse. // Sekoddeśa_89 //
and
speech in the secret [center], body at the navel, from <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss);
<s>Dharmakāya</s>, <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s>, and <s>Nirmāṇakāya</s> radiate from the pure body. // Sekoddeśa_90 //

body.translated_text: In the jewel, mind,

children.translated_text: which
would be above;
the body-<s>vajra</s> at the forehead, of this [wisdom] at the throat, heart, and navel lotuses. // Sekoddeśa_91 //

body.translated_text: Below <s>upāya</s> (method), O king, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)

children.translated_text: The speech, mind, and wisdom <s>vajras</s> radiate from <s>Nirmāṇakāya</s> and so forth;
the radiation of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and <s>dhātus</s> (elements), from unobstructed bliss. // Sekoddeśa_92 //
Through the attainment of <s>karmamudrā</s> (action seal) and the supports of <s>jñānamudrā</s> (wisdom seal);
through the single yoga of <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal), that imperishable [bliss] increases. // Sekoddeśa_93 //

children.text: vṛddhasya na ca syāt vṛddhiḥ kṣīṇasya kṣīṇatā na ca /
children.translated_text: Of that which has grown, there would be no further growth; of that which has diminished, no further diminishing;
of that which has set, there is no setting; of that which has risen, there is indeed no rising. // Sekoddeśa_94 //

children.text: na prakāśaḥ prakāśasya pihitaṃ pihitasya na /
children.translated_text: There is no illumination of the illuminated, no concealment of the concealed;

children.text: jātasyaiva na janma syān mṛtasya maraṇaṃ na ca // Sekoddeśa_95 //
children.translated_text: of the born there would be no birth, and of the dead no death. // Sekoddeśa_95 //

children.text: muktasya na ca muktiḥ syādasthitasya ca cāsthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the liberated there would be no liberation, and of the unestablished no lack of establishment;

children.text: abhāvo na hyabhāvasya bhāvo bhāvasya naiva ca // Sekoddeśa_96 //
children.translated_text: there is indeed no non-existence of the non-existent, nor existence of the existent. // Sekoddeśa_96 //

children.text: kṣarasyāpi kṣaro na syādakṣarasya na cākṣaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the perishable there would be no perishability, and of the imperishable no imperishability;
for <s>dharmas</s> whose nature is non-existence, arising is illusion, and likewise destruction. // Sekoddeśa_97 //

children.text: na kṣayaṃ yānti bhūtāni na jāyante svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Beings do not go to destruction, nor are they born by their own nature;
this universe is without own-nature, characterized solely by existence and non-existence. // Sekoddeśa_98 //
The mind embraced by one's own <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), gone to the <s>vajramaṇi</s> (vajra jewel) in the lotus;
there, the vibration of the moon's movement—the meditation on the motionless imperishable. // Sekoddeśa_99 //
In the <s>nāḍīs</s> of body, speech, and mind, the meditation on body, speech, and mind;
the collection of the three <s>vajras</s>, the meditation on <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis) in the <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>. // Sekoddeśa_100 //
And of the <s>bindus</s> melted by the passion of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), from the head in sequence,
of those that have entered the state of fullness, the binding is in the ultimate sense. // Sekoddeśa_101 //

body.text:
yathoditaḥ kramāccandraḥ kalābhiryāti pūrṇatām /
vāsanāharaṇaṃ pūrṇā

children.translated_text: not
a cutting of the moon, nor a filling. // Sekoddeśa_102 //

body.translated_text: Just as the moon, having risen, goes to fullness through its digits, the removal of <s>vāsanās</s> (habitual tendencies) is the fullness—

body.text:
tathoditaṃ kramājjñānaṃ bhūmibhiryāti pūrṇatām /
kleśādyāharaṇaṃ pūrṇā

children.translated_text: not
a cutting of knowledge, nor a filling. // Sekoddeśa_103 //

body.translated_text: Likewise, <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), having arisen, goes to fullness through the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages); the removal of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and so forth is the fullness—

children.text: yathā madhyaśaśāṅkena pūrṇāyāṃ na sthiraḥ śaśī /
children.translated_text: Just as by the mark on the moon, at the full moon the hare is not steady,
so too by the mark of <s>saṃsāric</s> habitual tendencies, the mind [is not steady] in imperishable bliss. // Sekoddeśa_104 //
bright
and dark, established;

children.text: tayormadhye tu yā pūrṇā sā pūrṇā na pratiṣṭhitā // Sekoddeśa_105 //
children.translated_text: but that fullness which is between those two, that fullness is not established. // Sekoddeśa_105 //

body.translated_text: Arising, dissolution; the fortnight—

children.translated_text: Fully awakened in a single moment, it would be motionless at the full [moon];

children.text: yadā vajramaṇau citaṃ tat sarvakṣaṇapūrakam // Sekoddeśa_106 //
children.translated_text: when the mind is in the <s>vajramaṇi</s> (vajra jewel), that fills all moments. // Sekoddeśa_106 //

children.text: na sthitiḥ śuklapakṣe 'sya gamanaṃ nāsite kvacit /
children.translated_text: There is no abiding in the bright fortnight for this, nor movement in the dark anywhere;
abiding in the middle of the two fortnights, at the full moon, gone to non-duality. // Sekoddeśa_107 //

body.text:
uṣṇīṣādudayaṃ tasya pūrṇā vajramaṇau bhavet /
savirāgāt kalāhāni

children.translated_text: from the <s>vajra</s> station, complete fullness. // Sekoddeśa_108 //

body.translated_text: Its rising from the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, fullness would be in the <s>vajramaṇi</s> (vajra jewel); from dispassion, the diminishing of the <s>kalās</s> (digits)—

children.text: uṣṇīse hyudayo bhūyaḥ pūrṇā vajramaṇau punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> indeed is the rising again, fullness in the <s>vajramaṇi</s> (vajra jewel) once more;
from the absence of passion, there is loss of the digits (<s>kalā</s>); [but] there is no loss of <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis) for embodied beings. // Sekod 109 //
that is celebrated by the word 'full' (<s>pūrṇa</s>);
all other states of being are the causes of creation and dissolution. // Sekod 110 //

body.translated_text: Whose nature is <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss) —

children.translated_text: From [conditioned] existence one goes to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and from that one returns again to [conditioned] existence;

children.text: svapakṣābhyāṃ yathāṃ candro 'yanābhyāṃ bhāskaro yathā // Sekoddeśa_111 //
children.translated_text: just as the moon [waxes and wanes] by its own two halves, just as the sun [moves] by its two courses (<s>ayana</s>). // Sekod 111 //
When [the digit is] full, the fullness of the motionless [mind] is through the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>),
by twenty [thousand] two hundred and eight hundred breaths consumed by the imperishable moments (<s>akṣara-kṣaṇa</s>). // Sekod 112 //
Having transcended the two halves [of the lunar cycle], [the mind is] filled by the stages;
the twelve-aspected truth-meaning, and the sixteen-aspected imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>). // Sekod 113 //
The twelve-aspected [truth] filled by the stages, the supreme non-dual;
the mind filled by the digits (<s>kalā</s>), the sixteen-aspected imperishable. // Sekod 114 //
The single-meaning, non-dual <s>dharma</s>, the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>), indestructible;

children.text: pūrṇāvasthāṃ gataṃ cittaṃ āsamantāt prapūritam // Sekoddeśa_115 //
children.translated_text: the mind that has reached the state of fullness (<s>pūrṇāvasthā</s>), completely filled on all sides. // Sekod 115 //
[of the lunar cycle]. // Sekod 116 //

body.translated_text: From dispassion [arises] the great passion (<s>mahārāga</s>), the bodiless <s>vajra</s> (<s>vajrānaṅga</s>), the great imperishable (<s>mahākṣara</s>), completely full, unafflicted, by the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the two halves

body.text:
yathā nadyudakaṃ viṣṭaṃ samudre tatpayaḥsamam /
tathā bhāvasamūho 'yamakṣare tatsamo

children.translated_text: imperishable. // Sekod 117 //

body.translated_text: Just as river-water poured into the ocean becomes equal to that [ocean] water, so this aggregate of [conditioned] states, in the imperishable, becomes equal to that —

children.translated_text: when consumed [by mercury], attains the state of mercury (<s>rasatva</s>);

children.text: bījairbījasva bhāvaṃ ca phalakāle mānavarjitam // Sekoddeśa_118 //
children.translated_text: and seeds [attain] the nature of seeds, and at the time of fruition [are] free from measure — // Sekod 118 //

body.translated_text: Just as this collection of [base] metals,

children.translated_text: so too, the aggregate of [conditioned] states, consumed by the supreme imperishable (<s>paramākṣara</s>),
attains the state of the supreme imperishable, bearing the form of all aspects. // Sekod 119 //

children.text: na daṃśe vedanāṃ vetti nānyatra cāpi daṣṭakaḥ /
children.translated_text: One bitten [by a snake] does not feel sensation at the [place of the] bite, nor elsewhere;

children.text: na viṣayānindriyadvāraiḥ pūrṇāvasthāṃ viṣe gate // Sekoddeśa_120 //
children.translated_text: [he does] not [perceive] sense-objects through the gates of the senses, when the poison has reached the state of fullness. // Sekod 120 //

children.text: evaṃ na ca maṇau yogī nānyatra vetti satsukham /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the yogin [does not feel] in the jewel [i.e., the maṇi-cakra] nor elsewhere the true bliss;
[he does] not [perceive] sense-objects through the gates of the senses, when the mind has reached the full digit (<s>pūrṇa-kalā</s>). // Sekod 121 //
Just as the great mercury (<s>mahārasa</s>), stationed even in one spot of [base] metal,
transmutes the metal intensely heated by fire on all sides — // Sekod 122 //
so too, the imperishable bliss, stationed even in one spot,
transmutes the mind intensely heated by the fire of desire on all sides. // Sekod 123 //

children.text: yathā ca viddhalohānāṃ naiva malo bhavet kvacit /
children.translated_text: And just as there is never any impurity in transmuted metals,

children.text: tathā ca viddhacittānāṃ na vāsanā bhavet kvacit // Sekoddeśa_124 //
children.translated_text: so too there is never any latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) in transmuted minds. // Sekod 124 //

children.text: hematvaṃ hi gataṃ lohamagninā nirmalaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Metal that has attained the state of gold becomes pure through fire;

children.text: bhūyo bhūyastathā cittaṃ nirmalaṃ rāgavahninā // Sekoddeśa_125 //
children.translated_text: likewise, again and again, the mind [becomes] pure through the fire of passion. // Sekod 125 //
Just as by the touch of a great jewel, stone attains radiance,
so by the touch of imperishable bliss (<s>akṣara-sukha</s>), the mind attains [the state of] bliss. // Sekod 126 //
What need is there to say much? From the standpoint of conventional truth (<s>lokasaṃvṛti-satya</s>),
the existence of mercury is beyond reasoning with respect to the transmutation of metal. // Sekod 127 //
The existence of <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis) is [even more] beyond reasoning; how much more so from the standpoint of ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>),
with respect to the transmutation of the mind that is smeared with adventitious defilements? // Sekod 128 //
The defilement in the mind is not adventitious, nor is it of long duration from the mind;

children.text: na cittena vinā jāto na citte saṃsthito 'vyayaḥ // Sekoddeśa_129 //
children.translated_text: it is not born apart from the mind, nor does it abide in the mind as imperishable. // Sekod 129 //
If it were merely adventitious, then the mind would be previously without defilement;

children.text: cirakālī yadā cittāttasyaiva sambhavaḥ kutaḥ // Sekoddeśa_130 //
children.translated_text: [if it is] of long duration, then how [can there be] its arising from the mind itself? // Sekod 130 //

children.text: yadi cittaṃ vinā jātastadā khakusumaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: If it were born apart from the mind, then [it would be] like a sky-flower;

children.text: yadi sthitaḥ sadā citte na naśyet sarvatastadā // Sekoddeśa_131 //
children.translated_text: if it always abides in the mind, then it would never be destroyed from any [direction]. // Sekod 131 //
Just as the blackness of copper is destroyed by the application of mercury,

children.text: na tasya sattvatā naśyennirmalatvena yā sthitā // Sekoddeśa_132 //
children.translated_text: its essential nature (<s>sattvatā</s>) does not perish — that which abides as purity. // Sekod 132 //
Likewise, the defilement of the mind is destroyed by the application of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>);

children.text: na tasya jñānatā naśyennirmalatvena yā sthitā // Sekoddeśa_133 //
children.translated_text: its nature as <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis) does not perish — that which abides as purity. // Sekod 133 //

children.text: rasaviddho yathā loho na punarlohatāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: Just as metal transmuted by mercury would never return to the state of [base] metal,

children.text: sukhaviddhaṃ tathā cittaṃ na punarduḥkhatāṃ vrajet // Sekoddeśa_134 //
children.translated_text: so too, the mind transmuted by bliss would never return to the state of suffering. // Sekod 134 //

children.text: na virāgāt paraṃ pāpaṃ na puṇyaṃ sukhataḥ param /
children.translated_text: There is no sin greater than the absence of passion (<s>virāga</s>), no merit greater than bliss;

children.text: ato 'kṣarasukhe cittaṃ veśanīyaṃ sadā nṛpa // Sekoddeśa_135 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one should always cause the mind to enter imperishable bliss (<s>akṣara-sukha</s>), O king. // Sekod 135 //

children.text: vaktuṃ na śakyate saukhyaṃ kumāryā surataṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: The happiness of a maiden cannot be told without sexual union;

children.text: yauvane surataṃ prāpya svato vetti mahāsukham // Sekoddeśa_136 //
children.translated_text: having attained sexual union in youth, she knows <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss) by herself. // Sekod 136 //

children.text: evaṃ na śakyate vaktuṃ samādhirahitaiḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: Likewise, bliss cannot be told by those devoid of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption);

children.text: samādhāvakṣaraṃ prāpya svato vindanti yoginaḥ // Sekoddeśa_137 //
children.translated_text: having attained the imperishable in <s>samādhi</s>, yogins find [it] by themselves. // Sekod 137 //
Regarding the knowledge of the bliss born of the imperishable — even by the omniscient ones (<s>sarvajña</s>) it is [only] surmised;

children.text: tathā kvacinna kartavyo virāgo manaso 'sukhāt // Sekoddeśa_138 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one should never anywhere produce dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) from the mind's unhappiness. // Sekod 138 //
From the emission [of bodhicitta], the arising of dispassion; from dispassion, the arising of suffering;

children.text: duḥkhāddhātukṣayaḥ puṃsāṃ kṣayān mṛtyuriti smṛtaḥ // Sekoddeśa_139 //
children.translated_text: from suffering, the decay of the <s>dhātus</s> (bodily elements) of men; from decay, death — so it is declared. // Sekod 139 //
From death, rebirth for those [beings]; from [conditioned] existence, death and emission again;

children.text: evaṃ virāgasaṃbhūteḥ sattvānāṃ nānyathā bhavaḥ // Sekoddeśa_140 //
children.translated_text: thus, from the arising of dispassion, there is no other [mode of] existence for beings. // Sekod 140 //
Therefore, with every effort, one should abandon the passion of emission (<s>cyuti-rāga</s>);
by which the yogin goes to imperishable bliss from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Sekod 141 //
Even a sensualist (<s>kāmuka</s>) does not desire the <s>kāmaśāstra</s> (treatise on desire) out of dispassion;

children.text: mayokte kiṃ punastantre yogī duḥkhaṃ samīhate // Sekoddeśa_142 //
children.translated_text: how much less would a yogin in the <s>tantra</s> taught by me desire suffering? // Sekod 142 //
By the nature of the imperishable semen (<s>śukrākṣara</s>), one should accomplish the supreme imperishable;
when the support [i.e., the body] undergoes emission, there is dispassion for the supported [i.e., the mind]. // Sekod 143 //
As long as the relationship of support and supported does not attain the state of the imperishable,
the mind that has attained the state of the imperishable has no characteristic of support and supported. // Sekod 144 //
For the body born of the imperishable, which has reached the <s>ūrṇā</s>-<s>cakra</s> (brow-wheel),
the union of the vowel and consonant series (<s>āli-kāli</s>) — the syllable <s>HŪṂ</s> — is not desired, O king. // Sekod 145 //
The image born of emptiness is the cause; the fruit is the bliss born of the imperishable;

children.text: phalena mudrito heturhetunā mudritaṃ phalam // Sekoddeśa_146 //
children.translated_text: the cause is sealed by the fruit, and the fruit is sealed by the cause. // Sekod 146 //
Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), bearing the image, is the cause; compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), bearing the imperishable, is the fruit;
<s>Bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind) is the inseparability of emptiness and compassion — that is the imperishable (<s>acyuta</s>). // Sekod 147 //
The image is free from <s>nirvāṇa</s>; the imperishable transcends <s>saṃsāra</s>;
free from eternalism and annihilationism — therefore, their yoga is the supreme non-dual. // Sekod 148 //
There is no non-existence of the image, since its characteristic arises from non-existence;
there is no existence of the imperishable either, since its characteristic arises from existence. // Sekod 149 //
The union of existence and non-existence is the <s>vajra</s>-yoga, the supreme non-dual,
free from form and formlessness — like a reflection in a mirror-divination. // Sekod 150 //
The image does not come into [conditioned] existence, nor does the imperishable [come into] <s>nirvāṇa</s>;
mutually embraced, quiescent — the supreme state of neither [male nor female] (<s>napuṃsaka-pada</s>). // Sekod 151 //
Because [the fruit is] unborn from the cause of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the fruit is born from the cause of wisdom;
because [it is] unborn from the cause of wisdom, what is born from wisdom is not born from a [conventional] cause. // Sekod 152 //
Therefore, <s>jñāna</s> (gnosis) is not born from a cause — the wisdom-knowledge (<s>prajñā-jñāna</s>) is unsurpassed;
by the fruit and by the cause mutually, there is no mutual sealing. // Sekod 153 //

children.text: hetuḥ phalaṃ ca yat sarvaṃ tat pratītyasamudbhavam /
children.translated_text: Whatever is cause and fruit, all that is dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamudbhava</s>);

children.text: anyonyamudritaṃ bimbaṃ notpannaṃ na ca nirvṛtam // Sekoddeśa_154 //
children.translated_text: the image, mutually sealed, is neither arisen nor ceased. // Sekod 154 //
Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is utterly ceased; and the supreme imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) is arisen;
[yet] the freedom from cause and fruit — there is no mutual sealing. // Sekod 155 //
The seeing here of the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) that is unborn and unceased —
that is of one's own mind, not of another, [as known] from the division of external knowables. // Sekod 156 //

children.text: ato na cātmanātmānaṃ mudrituṃ śakyate kvacit /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one can never seal oneself by oneself;
does the great sword cut itself with its own edge? // Sekod 157 //
Just as in a dream, bliss arises from union with a barren woman's daughter,
so [is the bliss arising] from cultivating oneself with the image born of space. // Sekod 158 //

children.text: na prajñā nāpyupāyo 'sau sahajaḥ prajñayā saha /
children.translated_text: It is neither wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) nor method (<s>upāya</s>) — [it is] innate (<s>sahaja</s>) together with wisdom,
and filled with bliss, free from all obscurations. // Sekod 159 //
Like space, free from obscuration, devoid of sense-objects and sense-faculties,
present in all beings everywhere, indivisible, free from differentiation. // Sekod 160 //
That self-born <s>Vajrasattva</s>, of great meaning, the supreme imperishable,
the great passion (<s>mahārāga</s>), the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), the one who creates delight for all beings. // Sekod 161 //
<s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great hatred (<s>mahādveṣa</s>), the destroyer of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), the great enemy [of defilements];
<s>Samayasattva</s>, the great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>), the subduer of the delusion of deluded minds. // Sekod 162 //
<s>Vajrayoga</s>, the great wrath (<s>mahākrodha</s>), the great enemy of the wrathful <s>Māra</s>;
<s>Kālacakra</s>, the great greed (<s>mahālobha</s>), the slayer of the greed of the perishable. // Sekod 163 //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> here declares the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) to be indestructible, of great meaning;
Being (<s>sattva</s>) is the oneness of the three realms of existence -- that is called the supreme syllable (<s>paramākṣara</s>). [164]
Filled with the bliss of the <s>paramākṣara</s> (supreme imperishable), perfected through the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>),
He is <s>mahārāga</s> (great passion), <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being), who brings delight to all beings. [165]
The being established in awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is a <s>bodhisattva</s>, therefore immovable;
He is <s>mahādveṣa</s> (great aversion), the great enemy of the hosts of hatred toward <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and the rest. [166]
The <s>samaya</s> (commitment) is the lunar nectar, the seminal fluid; <s>acyuti</s> (non-falling) is its consumption;
The <s>samayasattva</s> (commitment-being), by this practice, is the destroyer of the delusion of the deluded mind. [167]
The oneness of all <s>vajras</s> together with the syllables of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>kāya</s> (body) --
He is <s>mahākrodha</s> (great wrath), the great foe of the <s>Māras</s> who take the form of wrath. [168]
Through the means of the bliss of the great imperishable (<s>mahākṣara</s>), one should never abandon the welfare of beings;
He is <s>mahālobha</s> (great greed) to liberate beings, the destroyer of perishable greed. [169]
These six aspects (<s>ṣaḍākāra</s>) have been declared as the imperishable gnosis-experience (<s>akṣarajñānavedanā</s>);
Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) -- these are the families of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). [170]
Gnosis (<s>jñāna</s>), fire, space, earth, wind, and water, in due order,
And likewise mind, eye, ear, body, nose, and tongue; [171]
Sound, taste, <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of reality), smell, touch, and form --

children.text: krodharāṭ ṣaṇmukho bhīmaḥ ṣaṭkulaiḥ pariśodhitaḥ // Sekoddeśa_172 //
children.translated_text: The wrathful king (<s>krodharāṭ</s>), terrifying, six-faced, is purified by the six families. [172]
Body, secret, sense-faculty, and mind -- the threefold <s>maṇḍala</s> is ever-present;
From the triple <s>vajras</s> of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means), <s>vajrasattva</s>-hood arises. [173]
This is the practice of the consecration (<s>seka</s>), the realization of the <s>paramākṣara</s> (supreme imperishable);
Endowed with the system of <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) and families, it has been spoken in summary (<s>uddeśa</s>) from the lunar [tantra]. [174]
Thus concludes the glorious <s>Sekoddeśa</s> (Summary of the Consecration).
